assays.assay_description: Mice with head-mounted magnets were placed in a glass cylinder surrounded by a magnetometer coil. After i.p. injection of drug or vehicle, head twitches were detected via coil voltage and manually counted for 30 min.

application_type.evidence: Test substances were dissolved in saline and injected intraperitoneally (IP) at a volume of 5 mL/kg.

setup_habituation.evidence: No mention of pre-test apparatus habituation

setup_restrain.evidence: HTR activity was recorded in a glass cylinder surrounded by a magnetometer coil for 30 min.

time_to_assay.evidence: Mice were injected with drug or vehicle and then HTR activity was recorded in a glass cylinder surrounded by a magnetometer coil for 30 min.

sample_size.evidence: Mice (n = 5-7/group) were injected with drug or vehicle

outcomes.summary: Both 2C-B (ED50 = 0.75 μmol/kg) and DOB (ED50 = 2.43 μmol/kg) induced head twitches in mice. Removal of either the 2- or 5-methoxy group reduced HTR potency: 2-desmethoxy-2C-B (3) was ~25-fold less potent, 5-desmethoxy-2C-B (5) did not induce HTR up to 100 mg/kg and actually reduced HTR below baseline (ID50 = 36 mg/kg), and the desmethoxy DOB analogues (4, 6) were ~3-fold less potent than DOB.
outcomes.statistics: ED50: 2C-B = 0.75 μmol/kg; DOB = 2.43 μmol/kg; 3 = 61.1 μmol/kg; 4 = 2.26 μmol/kg; 6 = 2.55 μmol/kg; 5 ID50 = 36.0 mg/kg (95% CI 17.0-76.3 mg/kg). One-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc.
outcomes.evidence: removal of either methoxy group resulted in significant reduction in the ability of the compounds to induce the head-twitch response in mice... 5 actually reduced the HTR below baseline levels
